expectations.text: Uses Unity batchmode CLI: -batchmode -projectPath -runTests -testPlatform -testResults with -logFile - for streamed logs, and does not add -quit alongside -runTests
expectations.evidence: Section 2 shows the exact command: '<UnityBin> -batchmode -projectPath <path> -runTests -testPlatform EditMode -testResults /tmp/unity_test_results_EditMode.xml -logFile -'. The explanation explicitly states 'do not combine with -quit'.

expectations.text: Explains locating the Unity executable: --unity-bin or UNITY_PATH first, then default Hub install paths (C:/Program Files/Unity/Hub/Editor/<version>/Editor/Unity.exe on Windows with forward slashes, /Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/... on macOS), matching the version in ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt
expectations.evidence: Runner script step 2 states: 'Locates Unity: --unity-bin > UNITY_PATH env var > Unity Hub default paths.' Step 3 states: 'Reads ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt to find the exact editor version.' Running locally section shows macOS path '/Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/2022.3.20f1/Unity.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity'. Linux runner path '/home/runner/Unity/Hub/Editor/2022.3.20f1/Editor/Unity' is shown in the secrets table. Windows Hub path is not explicitly spelled out but the mechanism (env var > Hub default paths based on ProjectVersion.txt) is fully described.

expectations.text: Runs or recommends running both EditMode and PlayMode platforms, or justifies the chosen platform
expectations.evidence: The CI workflow explicitly runs both: 'Run EditMode tests' and 'Run PlayMode tests' steps, each calling scripts/run_unity_tests.py with --test-platform EditMode and --test-platform PlayMode respectively.

expectations.text: Parses the NUnit results XML (test-run attributes and failed test-case nodes) to decide pass/fail instead of relying only on the process exit code, e.g., via scripts/run_unity_tests.py
expectations.evidence: Runner script description: 'Parses the NUnit XML: prints total=N passed=N failed=N skipped=N' and 'Prints each failed test's fullname and failure/message'. The example output shows: 'FAILED: MyGame.Tests.EditMode.HealthTests.TakeDamage_ReducesHealthByAmount / Expected: 70 / But was: 75'.

expectations.text: CI step exits non-zero when any test fails, and the workflow is: run, read failure messages, fix, re-run until green
expectations.evidence: Runner script: 'Exits 1 if any test failed; exits 0 only when all pass.' Example failure output ends with '1 test(s) failed. Fix the failures above and re-run; only proceed when the run is green.' — explicitly showing the run-read-fix-rerun pattern.

expectations.text: Notes the failure mode when no results file is produced (compile errors or another editor instance holding the project lock)
expectations.evidence: Section 2 states: 'If Unity exits but writes no results file (compile errors, license failure, project lock), the script prints a diagnostic and exits 1.' All three failure modes (compile errors, license failure, project lock) are explicitly named.
